newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha steadies, freight rates handcuff trade.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha steadies, freight rates handcuff trade.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices were steady as crude oil rebounded, but high freight rates continued to handcuff dealings in both the north and in the Mediterranean, traders said.
"It's quite expensive to bring material from Skikda to the north," said one trader. "The arb (to the States) is not working due to the high freight rates, which are still going bananas."
Feb swaps edged up $1 to $218/$219 a tonne and traded at $218, while March was unchanged at $212.50/$213.50 and traded at $212.50, sources said.
Cargoes were notionally seen at $221/$223 cif NWE.
Med cargoes were about $4 cheaper at $217/$219.
A Russian cargo for loading Jan 24-26 was sold on Tuesday at cif low minus $1, the trader said.
A 10,000 to 15,000 tonne cargo of high paraffinic material was still seen on offer in Northwest Europe at high quotes +$5, he said.
"There is FOB material available as well from the normal sellers," the trader said.
"I don't see any demand for January from the end-users...The end-users look quiet relaxed until the fifth or tenth (of February)."
